H_hierarchical.evidence: The paper gives a flat FSM with INIT_STATE, PRE_DETECTION, and DETECTION; no parent state, nested mode, or composite sub-FSM is described.

G_guards_arith.evidence: Detection is allowed only under the conjunction Reverse gear ON AND |Steering angle| <= 10 degrees AND Speed <= 5 km/h; the warning trigger also compares Bayesian discriminant/probability values.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: The DETECTION state continuously runs the vision pipeline, computes STHOL/Bayesian classification, and triggers a driver warning when oncoming-traffic likelihood exceeds free-traffic likelihood.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: The paper describes normal activation/deactivation conditions but no fault, emergency-stop, rollback, abort, or recovery path.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: FSM state names and CAN-Bus guards are in Section III/Fig. 4, while the DETECTION warning semantics are explained separately in the Bayesian detection sections.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Terms such as detection module, reverse gear, speed, steering angle, and warning are accompanied by explicit triggering conditions rather than requiring unstated domain rules.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: The action associated with DETECTION is not just the Fig. 4 label Warning; prose later explains that STHOL features and Bayesian discriminants decide when to trigger the warning signal.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: Condition 1 combines gear, absolute steering angle, and speed with boolean conjunction and threshold comparisons.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: No composite state or parent-state entry/during/exit behavior is present.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: The stop/deactivation condition is normal operating logic, not a global from-any-state fault or recovery rule.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: No composite state or initialization pseudo-chain is described.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: There is a meaningful multi-variable guard over reverse gear, speed, and steering angle, plus a numeric Bayesian warning threshold, but not three separate arithmetic-boolean guards.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: No cross-cutting rule applies to multiple substates, and there is no parent-level during action over a composite state.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: The controller triggers a driver warning signal and activates/deactivates a detection module without committing to a concrete actuator or I/O channel.

key_nl_quotes: A Finite State Machine (FSM) defined according to three CAN-Bus variables and a manual signal provided by the user is used to handle the activation/deactivation of the detection module.
The system stops if one of the following conditions are met: vehicle speed is greater than 5km/h, steering angle is greater than 10 degrees, or reverse gear is deactivated.
one_line_pitch: A flat but guard-heavy ADAS FSM whose DETECTION state couples multi-variable CAN-Bus activation logic with an implicitly attached probabilistic warning action.
rationale: This is a strong guard/action stress test: the FSM itself is small, but DETECTION depends on a multi-variable conjunction over gear, speed, and steering angle, and its warning action is defined through a separate Bayesian vision pipeline. It has no hierarchy or fault recovery, so it is not broad across all four H/G/A/F axes, but it directly targets the guard and action weaknesses reported for prior Umple-style baselines. The cross-section split between FSM definition and warning semantics also creates a real baseline-trap density.
